title: Why the band was called jungle music
summary: Greer denies that Ellington wanted to rename jazz but says Gershwin called their music jungle music at the Cotton Club.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Duke Ellington said once that there was -- he was attempting to get the guys to change the name of the music from jazz to Negro music when you all got to New York. Do you remember that?
No. No, that never come up. What did

come up, the real truth about it, we played -- I don't know how it originated or nothing like that, but somebody -- I don't know whether it was Paul Whiteman because he idolized Duke or Gershwin. He was a steady customer at the Cotton Club.

They used to -- of the things in awe, Duke used to do, so they were sitting up at the Cotton Club and George Gershwin said to Paul, I know what that is, that's jungle music. And it stuck with us. Stuck with us. But never, never, they would never say that because a lot of the guys up there, they may say you guys but they was scared to offend a guy's feelings, and you know, with all respect, the jungle music, and that latched on to us.
